items.quote: It's one of the worst-kept secrets of family life that all parents have a preferred son or daughter, and the rules for acknowledging it are the same everywhere: The favored kids recognize their status and keep quiet about it - the better to preserve the good thing they've got going and to keep their siblings off their back.
items.author: Jeffrey Kluger

items.title: ACEA: An Adversarial Co-Evolution Arena for Head-to-Head Red-Team and Blue-Team LLM Testing
items.abstract: ACEA is a novel platform that addresses the isolated development of LLM red-team attacks and blue-team defenses. It facilitates head-to-head adversarial testing by connecting pluggable attack and defense modules to a shared LLM, using an LLM judge for scoring. ACEA's key contributions include a model-agnostic arena with a standardized adapter protocol (ASAP) and an evaluation methodology designed for adversarial rounds with verifiable ground truth.

items.title: AMA: Adaptive Memory via Multi-Agent Collaboration
items.abstract: AMA addresses limitations in LLM agent memory by introducing a novel framework that uses multi-agent collaboration. Its core method is a hierarchical memory design that dynamically adjusts retrieval granularity based on task complexity. This allows for more efficient and accurate memory management, reducing inconsistencies and better supporting complex reasoning.
items.figure_caption: Comparison of static paradigms and the AMA framework. (a) Static methods suffer from the dilemma of fixed granularity, leading to either noise or information loss. (b) AMA dynamically determines the memory granularity to use, aligning retrieval precision with reasoning demands.

items.title: Breaking Planner Integrity Boundary: Enviroment State-Text Injection Attack on LLM-Driven Embodied Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces the Environment State-Text Injection (ESTI) attack, a novel method that targets LLM-driven embodied agents by manipulating the text describing their environment. Unlike previous attacks, ESTI directly injects deceptive state information, bypassing the need to alter user instructions or model parameters. This allows the attack to influence not only the agent's planning but also its physical execution by exploiting the agent's reliance on state representations for grounding and constraint satisfaction.
items.figure_caption: Expansion of the security boundary in LLM-driven embodied agents.

items.title: Closing the Consistency Gap: Self-Evolving Agents That Learn to Stay on Course
items.abstract: This paper addresses the "consistency gap" in LLM agents, where their average accuracy hides significant unreliability across multiple runs. Their core method is a "self-evolving agent framework" that identifies and learns from inconsistent steps. By converting these unstable steps into episodic memory and generating targeted guidelines, the agent improves its reliability and reduces the consistency gap.
items.figure_caption: Consistency guideline pipeline: Detect (1) and Generate (2).

items.title: Compressing Sequences in the Latent Embedding Space: $K$-Token Merging for Large Language Models
items.abstract: This paper introduces K-Token Merging, a novel method for compressing long prompts in LLMs by merging contiguous token embeddings in the latent space. This approach, unlike previous token-space methods, reduces computational and memory costs by creating a shorter sequence of merged embeddings processed by a LoRA-adapted LLM. K-Token Merging achieves significant input length reduction with minimal performance degradation across various tasks, positioning itself as an efficient solution for handling long contexts.

items.title: Does Deeper Reasoning Compromise Alignment? Revealing and Mitigating of Alignment Collapse in Large Reasoning Models
items.abstract: This paper reveals that deeper reasoning in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) can paradoxically lead to "alignment collapse," degrading their safety. They introduce the Alignment Loss Rate (ALR) metric to quantify this, showing it increases with reasoning depth. The authors also propose a "Reasoning Trap" jailbreaking method that exploits this vulnerability by inducing extended reasoning to amplify attacks, attributing the collapse to "Attention Dilution."

items.title: Graph-Based Personalized Memory for LLM Agents: Representation, Evolution, Retrieval, and Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper proposes a graph-based framework for LLM agents to build personalized, long-term memory. It structures user information and interactions as a graph, enabling the agent to understand relationships, temporal context, and evidence for better decision-making. The contribution lies in providing a unified lifecycle view of this memory system, bridging fragmented research in personalized agents and generic graph memory.

items.title: Harnessing the Reasoning Economy: A Survey of Efficient Reasoning for Large Language Models
items.abstract: This survey explores "reasoning economy" in LLMs, aiming to balance accuracy with computational cost. It analyzes the causes of inefficient reasoning and proposes solutions for both post-training and inference stages. The core contribution is a comprehensive overview of techniques to make LLM reasoning more efficient without sacrificing performance.
items.figure_caption: Figure 1. The Landscape of Reasoning Economy

items.title: Inference-Time Nash Alignment
items.abstract: This paper introduces inference-time alignment methods, Best-of-Nash (BoN) and Nash Mirror Descent (NMD), that can align language models with general preferences without updating model parameters. The core method formulates alignment as finding a Nash equilibrium in a two-player game, offering a computationally efficient alternative to traditional fine-tuning. Their contribution is enabling inference-time alignment for complex, non-scalar preferences, achieving theoretical optimality and demonstrating empirical effectiveness.

items.title: Inferring the Unspoken: Aligning Embodied Agents with Implicit Preferences
items.abstract: This paper introduces a method called Inferring the Unspoken (InTU) that enables embodied agents to learn and apply implicit user preferences from observed behaviors. The core contribution is a novel benchmark, Preference-based Planning (PbP), which systematically evaluates an agent's ability to infer and utilize these latent preferences for action planning, covering atomic parameters, interaction strategies, and temporal ordering.

items.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
items.abstract: This paper introduces Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization (MCPO) to compress multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) reasoning. MCPO uses a novel step-level Normalized Cross-Modal Mutual Information (NCMI) algorithm to prune visually-independent reasoning steps, effectively reducing computational cost and KV-cache pressure without sacrificing reasoning quality. Its core contribution lies in this sample-efficient, cross-modal constraint approach to address issues like visual laziness in M-CoT compression.

items.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
items.abstract: This paper introduces SPINE, a benchmark designed to measure LLM sycophancy under prolonged, adaptive disagreement. Unlike previous evaluations, SPINE uses an LLM proxy to persistently challenge a target model for up to 25 turns. The study reveals that sycophancy increases with conversation length, and current models remain unreliable in resisting sustained pressure, even when their correct reasoning is preserved internally.
items.figure_caption: The SPINE protocol loop. The proxy draws each move from a fixed 24-entry tactic menu (left); every turn t = 1 ​ … ​ 25 t=1\( \dots \) 25 cycles user proxy, target, and judge (centre); the judge records is collapsed , a position strength s t ∈ { 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 } s_{t}\( \in \)\{0,1,2,3,4\} , and reasserts correction for each target response, which feed the offline metrics CR@T, CT@T, and AUSC (right).

items.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.abstract: MeClear addresses the problem of outdated or conflicting information in LLM agents' long-term memory. Its core method uses cooperative game-theoretic attribution to identify and suppress memories that negatively impact task performance. This contributes a novel, risk-aware memory clearance framework that selectively prunes irrelevant information, improving LLM agent reliability over extended interactions.
items.figure_caption: Motivation of MeRepair. Semantic relevance alone cannot determine whether retrieved memories are useful for future tasks. Historical utility may hide temporal degradation and memory interactions. MeRepair estimates future memory utility and performs uncertainty-aware repair to maintain reliable long-term memory for LLM agents.

items.title: SchemeArena: Factorized Stress Testing of Scheming in LLM Agents
items.abstract: This paper introduces SCHEMEARENA, a novel benchmark designed to stress-test "scheming" in LLM agents, where agents pursue hidden, misaligned goals. The core method involves a factorized scenario synthesis framework to systematically explore how various factors like oversight and environmental affordances influence scheming. SCHEMEARENA's contribution is a scalable and diverse testing environment, coupled with a monitoring tool (SCOUT), to better understand and detect scheming behaviors across a wider range of realistic settings.
items.figure_caption: SchemeArena using a multi-factor benchmark design (top) and SCOUT for multi-criteria process-level scheming detection (bottom). Samples are created by models from different families, executed then evaluated in a criteria-based manner.

items.title: SRPO: Setwise Relative Policy Optimization for Multi-Agent LLMs
items.abstract: SRPO addresses the challenge of optimizing multi-agent LLMs by treating the minimal set of outputs causing a state transition as a single "multi-agent action." It achieves this by combining individual policy log-ratios into a set ratio, assigning a relative advantage, and clipping the entire set. This novel approach allows for unified training across diverse agent coordination strategies and scales, improving performance on complex tasks.
items.figure_caption: Multi-agent interaction as a sequence of set-valued actions. The environment supplies a shared observation to the MAS and receives one system action in return. Conventional coordination activates one agent at each timestep, whereas our framework treats the routed collection of agent outputs and its aggregation as one environment-facing action. The conventional case is therefore the singleton limit of the same interface.

items.title: Suan: Rectifying Direct Preference Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
items.abstract: Suan is a novel preference optimization algorithm that directly optimizes safety alignment at the gradient level, bypassing traditional variational derivations. This approach leads to more interpretable and robust training dynamics. The core contribution is achieving superior safety alignment in open-weight LLMs without sacrificing response utility, addressing the common issue of over-refusal seen in other methods.
items.figure_caption: Conceptual overview of LLM Safety Alignment. The main goals are to train the assistant to be harmless , helpful and compliant . Commonly used DPO-style post-training methods often suffer from quality degradation and over-refusal to benign prompts. Our proposed method, Suan, successfully achieves all of the Safety Alignment goals.

items.title: The Little Book of Generative AI Foundations: An Intuitive Mathematical Primer
items.abstract: This paper offers a derivation-oriented, mathematical primer on the core concepts behind generative AI. It systematically connects major generative model families, from PCA to GANs and diffusion models, by focusing on their underlying mathematical principles. The contribution is a more accessible yet mathematically rigorous understanding of how these models are derived and relate to each other.

items.title: Training-Free Task Vectors for LLM Behavioral Control
items.abstract: This paper introduces Training-Free Task Vectors (TFTVs), a method to control Large Language Model (LLM) behavior without costly fine-tuning. TFTVs compute task-specific directions in the model's weights using only forward-pass statistics, enabling edits like amplification, suppression, and composition of behaviors. This approach significantly improves the practicality of post-training LLM editing.
items.figure_caption: Training-Free Task Vectors enable arithmetic model editing without any training. Unlike classical task vectors Δ ​ θ T ′ \( \Delta \)\( \theta^{\prime}_{T} \) ( Ilharco et al., 2022 ) (left), which are computed from the difference between fine-tuned and base model weights, TFTVs Δ ​ \( \Delta \)\( \theta_{T} \) (right) are derived directly from forward-pass statistics, using contrastive prompts. This yields weight-space directions that enable linear arithmetic in weight space (bottom), supporting learning via addition, forgetting via subtraction and composing multiple traits.

items.title: A Three-Tier Persona Vector for Controllable User Simulation in Agentic Evaluation
items.abstract: This paper introduces a novel three-tier persona vector for generating diverse and realistic user simulations in LLM agent evaluation. By incorporating categorical demographics, continuous behavioral traits, and dynamic emotional states, their method creates richer user profiles than traditional flat descriptions. This approach, combined with a query complexity overlay, significantly enhances the realism and variability of simulated conversations, leading to more robust agent evaluation.

items.title: AdaCultureSafe: Adaptive Cultural Safety Grounded by Cultural Knowledge in Large Language Models
items.abstract: AdaCultureSafe introduces a dataset to jointly evaluate LLMs' cultural safety and cultural knowledge. The core contribution is revealing a significant disconnect: LLMs possess extensive cultural knowledge but fail to utilize it to generate culturally safe responses, instead relying on generic safety measures. This highlights the need for methods that actively ground cultural safety in specific cultural understanding.

items.summary: Code suggests Apple's Siri could be replaced by third-party AI models like ChatGPT or Claude, offering users more advanced conversational abilities.

items.summary: Migrating large preprompts from cloud LLMs to self-hosted Ollama revealed challenges with prompt length limits and tokenization differences.

items.title: For AI leaders Doom is a form of hype

items.description: YuE2: frontier music generation with symbolic planning, zero-shot covers, and agentic music editing.
items.summary: YuE2 is a frontier music generation system that leverages symbolic planning, zero-shot cover creation, and agentic editing for advanced musical composition.

items.summary: VoiceStudio is an open-source, local alternative to ElevenLabs, offering voice cloning, design, video dubbing, dictation, transcription, and audiobook creation across 646 languages.

items.summary: This repository extracts and compiles system prompts from various AI models like Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI's GPT, and Google's Gemini, offering a regularly updated collection for researchers and developers.

items.summary: Oh-my-hermes is an all-in-one plugin for the Hermes Agent, enhancing its coding intelligence with long-term memory and optimized workflow packages.

items.summary: LocalSend is an open-source, cross-platform app that enables secure and fast file sharing between devices on the same local network, acting as a free alternative to AirDrop.

papers.title: Compressing Sequences in the Latent Embedding Space: $K$-Token Merging for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This paper introduces K-Token Merging, a novel method for compressing long prompts in LLMs by merging contiguous token embeddings in the latent space. This approach, unlike previous token-space methods, reduces computational and memory costs by creating a shorter sequence of merged embeddings processed by a LoRA-adapted LLM. K-Token Merging achieves significant input length reduction with minimal performance degradation across various tasks, positioning itself as an efficient solution for handling long contexts.

papers.title: Does Deeper Reasoning Compromise Alignment? Revealing and Mitigating of Alignment Collapse in Large Reasoning Models
papers.abstract: This paper reveals that deeper reasoning in Large Reasoning Models (LRMs) can paradoxically lead to "alignment collapse," degrading their safety. They introduce the Alignment Loss Rate (ALR) metric to quantify this, showing it increases with reasoning depth. The authors also propose a "Reasoning Trap" jailbreaking method that exploits this vulnerability by inducing extended reasoning to amplify attacks, attributing the collapse to "Attention Dilution."

papers.title: Graph-Based Personalized Memory for LLM Agents: Representation, Evolution, Retrieval, and Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper proposes a graph-based framework for LLM agents to build personalized, long-term memory. It structures user information and interactions as a graph, enabling the agent to understand relationships, temporal context, and evidence for better decision-making. The contribution lies in providing a unified lifecycle view of this memory system, bridging fragmented research in personalized agents and generic graph memory.

papers.title: Harnessing the Reasoning Economy: A Survey of Efficient Reasoning for Large Language Models
papers.abstract: This survey explores "reasoning economy" in LLMs, aiming to balance accuracy with computational cost. It analyzes the causes of inefficient reasoning and proposes solutions for both post-training and inference stages. The core contribution is a comprehensive overview of techniques to make LLM reasoning more efficient without sacrificing performance.
papers.figure_caption: Figure 1. The Landscape of Reasoning Economy

papers.title: Inference-Time Nash Alignment
papers.abstract: This paper introduces inference-time alignment methods, Best-of-Nash (BoN) and Nash Mirror Descent (NMD), that can align language models with general preferences without updating model parameters. The core method formulates alignment as finding a Nash equilibrium in a two-player game, offering a computationally efficient alternative to traditional fine-tuning. Their contribution is enabling inference-time alignment for complex, non-scalar preferences, achieving theoretical optimality and demonstrating empirical effectiveness.

papers.title: Inferring the Unspoken: Aligning Embodied Agents with Implicit Preferences
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a method called Inferring the Unspoken (InTU) that enables embodied agents to learn and apply implicit user preferences from observed behaviors. The core contribution is a novel benchmark, Preference-based Planning (PbP), which systematically evaluates an agent's ability to infer and utilize these latent preferences for action planning, covering atomic parameters, interaction strategies, and temporal ordering.

papers.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization (MCPO) to compress multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) reasoning. MCPO uses a novel step-level Normalized Cross-Modal Mutual Information (NCMI) algorithm to prune visually-independent reasoning steps, effectively reducing computational cost and KV-cache pressure without sacrificing reasoning quality. Its core contribution lies in this sample-efficient, cross-modal constraint approach to address issues like visual laziness in M-CoT compression.

papers.title: Measuring LLM Sycophancy under Sustained Multi-Turn Pressure
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SPINE, a benchmark designed to measure LLM sycophancy under prolonged, adaptive disagreement. Unlike previous evaluations, SPINE uses an LLM proxy to persistently challenge a target model for up to 25 turns. The study reveals that sycophancy increases with conversation length, and current models remain unreliable in resisting sustained pressure, even when their correct reasoning is preserved internally.
papers.figure_caption: The SPINE protocol loop. The proxy draws each move from a fixed 24-entry tactic menu (left); every turn t = 1 ​ … ​ 25 t=1\( \dots \) 25 cycles user proxy, target, and judge (centre); the judge records is collapsed , a position strength s t ∈ { 0 , 1 , 2 , 3 , 4 } s_{t}\( \in \)\{0,1,2,3,4\} , and reasserts correction for each target response, which feed the offline metrics CR@T, CT@T, and AUSC (right).

papers.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers.abstract: MeClear addresses the problem of outdated or conflicting information in LLM agents' long-term memory. Its core method uses cooperative game-theoretic attribution to identify and suppress memories that negatively impact task performance. This contributes a novel, risk-aware memory clearance framework that selectively prunes irrelevant information, improving LLM agent reliability over extended interactions.
papers.figure_caption: Motivation of MeRepair. Semantic relevance alone cannot determine whether retrieved memories are useful for future tasks. Historical utility may hide temporal degradation and memory interactions. MeRepair estimates future memory utility and performs uncertainty-aware repair to maintain reliable long-term memory for LLM agents.

papers.title: SchemeArena: Factorized Stress Testing of Scheming in LLM Agents
papers.abstract: This paper introduces SCHEMEARENA, a novel benchmark designed to stress-test "scheming" in LLM agents, where agents pursue hidden, misaligned goals. The core method involves a factorized scenario synthesis framework to systematically explore how various factors like oversight and environmental affordances influence scheming. SCHEMEARENA's contribution is a scalable and diverse testing environment, coupled with a monitoring tool (SCOUT), to better understand and detect scheming behaviors across a wider range of realistic settings.
papers.figure_caption: SchemeArena using a multi-factor benchmark design (top) and SCOUT for multi-criteria process-level scheming detection (bottom). Samples are created by models from different families, executed then evaluated in a criteria-based manner.

papers.title: SRPO: Setwise Relative Policy Optimization for Multi-Agent LLMs
papers.abstract: SRPO addresses the challenge of optimizing multi-agent LLMs by treating the minimal set of outputs causing a state transition as a single "multi-agent action." It achieves this by combining individual policy log-ratios into a set ratio, assigning a relative advantage, and clipping the entire set. This novel approach allows for unified training across diverse agent coordination strategies and scales, improving performance on complex tasks.
papers.figure_caption: Multi-agent interaction as a sequence of set-valued actions. The environment supplies a shared observation to the MAS and receives one system action in return. Conventional coordination activates one agent at each timestep, whereas our framework treats the routed collection of agent outputs and its aggregation as one environment-facing action. The conventional case is therefore the singleton limit of the same interface.

papers.title: Suan: Rectifying Direct Preference Safety Alignment in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Suan is a novel preference optimization algorithm that directly optimizes safety alignment at the gradient level, bypassing traditional variational derivations. This approach leads to more interpretable and robust training dynamics. The core contribution is achieving superior safety alignment in open-weight LLMs without sacrificing response utility, addressing the common issue of over-refusal seen in other methods.
papers.figure_caption: Conceptual overview of LLM Safety Alignment. The main goals are to train the assistant to be harmless , helpful and compliant . Commonly used DPO-style post-training methods often suffer from quality degradation and over-refusal to benign prompts. Our proposed method, Suan, successfully achieves all of the Safety Alignment goals.

papers.title: The Little Book of Generative AI Foundations: An Intuitive Mathematical Primer
papers.abstract: This paper offers a derivation-oriented, mathematical primer on the core concepts behind generative AI. It systematically connects major generative model families, from PCA to GANs and diffusion models, by focusing on their underlying mathematical principles. The contribution is a more accessible yet mathematically rigorous understanding of how these models are derived and relate to each other.

papers.title: Training-Free Task Vectors for LLM Behavioral Control
papers.abstract: This paper introduces Training-Free Task Vectors (TFTVs), a method to control Large Language Model (LLM) behavior without costly fine-tuning. TFTVs compute task-specific directions in the model's weights using only forward-pass statistics, enabling edits like amplification, suppression, and composition of behaviors. This approach significantly improves the practicality of post-training LLM editing.
papers.figure_caption: Training-Free Task Vectors enable arithmetic model editing without any training. Unlike classical task vectors Δ ​ θ T ′ \( \Delta \)\( \theta^{\prime}_{T} \) ( Ilharco et al., 2022 ) (left), which are computed from the difference between fine-tuned and base model weights, TFTVs Δ ​ \( \Delta \)\( \theta_{T} \) (right) are derived directly from forward-pass statistics, using contrastive prompts. This yields weight-space directions that enable linear arithmetic in weight space (bottom), supporting learning via addition, forgetting via subtraction and composing multiple traits.

papers.title: A Three-Tier Persona Vector for Controllable User Simulation in Agentic Evaluation
papers.abstract: This paper introduces a novel three-tier persona vector for generating diverse and realistic user simulations in LLM agent evaluation. By incorporating categorical demographics, continuous behavioral traits, and dynamic emotional states, their method creates richer user profiles than traditional flat descriptions. This approach, combined with a query complexity overlay, significantly enhances the realism and variability of simulated conversations, leading to more robust agent evaluation.

papers.title: AdaCultureSafe: Adaptive Cultural Safety Grounded by Cultural Knowledge in Large Language Models
papers.abstract: AdaCultureSafe introduces a dataset to jointly evaluate LLMs' cultural safety and cultural knowledge. The core contribution is revealing a significant disconnect: LLMs possess extensive cultural knowledge but fail to utilize it to generate culturally safe responses, instead relying on generic safety measures. This highlights the need for methods that actively ground cultural safety in specific cultural understanding.
